system.name: RF-CHORD
system.one_liner: a deployable RFID localization system for logistics networks based on wideband active sniffing and kernel-based localization

components.name: Impinj Tx
components.role: commodity ISM-band reader transmitter that activates and coordinates access to EPC Gen II tags

components.name: Impinj reader
components.role: off-the-shelf reader that activates tags; exchanges no explicit information with the sniffer

components.name: Active sniffer
components.role: custom RF frontend + FPGA that emits a low-power wideband multi-sine signal and receives tag responses across 8 antennas and 16 frequencies

components.name: Demodulator
components.role: demodulates received channel samples into channel estimates

components.name: Kernel-layer based localization
components.role: computes a direct-path-enhanced location estimate from channel estimation and ROI info

components.name: ROI info
components.role: region-of-interest prior information supplied to the localization stage

flows.what: high power ISM signal that activates tags
low power wideband multisine tag response signal
channel samples from high-dynamic-range A/Ds and digital channelization into 16 channels
channel estimation, refined by full packet matching

content.key_idea: RF-CHORD passively sniffs the wideband multi-sine response of commodity RFID tags with a multi-antenna active sniffer, then digitally channelizes, packet-matches, and kernel-localizes the direct path using prior region-of-interest information to achieve accurate, long-range localization without exchanging information with the reader.
content.reading_order: left to right following seven numbered stages: high-power activation, low-power multisine response, high-dynamic-range sampling, digital channelization, full packet matching/demodulation, ROI-aided kernel localization, and the resulting direct-path-enhanced heatmap.

summary: This figure gives the end-to-end operational flow of RF-CHORD. A commodity Impinj reader/Tx emits a high-power ISM signal to activate EPC Gen II tags (step 1); tags respond with a low-power wideband multi-sine signal (step 2) captured by an active sniffer's multiple receive antennas and high-dynamic-range A/Ds (step 3), which digitally channelizes the signal into 16 frequency channels (step 4). A demodulator applies full packet matching to estimate the channel (step 5), and a kernel-layer localization stage combines this channel estimation with region-of-interest prior information to determine the direct path and suppress multipath/leakage (step 6), producing a direct-path-enhanced localization heatmap (step 7). Dashed callout boxes below the main pipeline expand on the multisine waveform, channelization, packet matching, and localization sub-steps.
